name: JumpCloud
one_liner: JumpCloud provides a cloud directory platform that manages user identities, access permissions, and devices across multiple operating systems.
what_you_sell: A cloud directory platform that unifies identity, access, and device management.
target_group: JumpCloud sells to small to mid-market companies, typically ranging from 20 to 1,000 employees, in cloud-centric industries like technology, digital services, and modern media. Good prospects have remote or hybrid workforces using a mix of operating systems (macOS, Windows, Linux) and cloud applications like Google Workspace. Bad prospects are legacy, on-premise, single-OS environments that do not manage remote access or multiple platforms.
who_uses_it: IT administrators, system specialists, and security engineers who manage user access and company devices.
who_pays_for_it: IT Directors, VPs of Infrastructure/IT, and Chief Information Security Officers (CISOs).
_claims_to_check: Claims active customers in over 160 countries.
Claims to natively govern autonomous AI agent identities alongside human identities.
Implies Google selected JumpCloud as their primary unified control plane partner.
